title: Contamination with osteoblasts of a bone marrow puncture (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: May-Grnwald-Giemsa (MGG). In bone marrow smears from a sternum puncture sometimes osteoblasts are found. Osteoblasts may occur in groups, are oval with a usually eccentric, relatively small nucleus. The chromatin is often coarse with 1-3 nucleoli. The cytoplasm is mostly light blue and may contain a few red granules. Osteoblasts are involved in formation of bone during remodelling and growth.

title: Bone | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: A high power view of bone being laid down on calcified cartilage. Osteoblasts are laying down bone and osteoclasts are remodeling it. Pale osteoid is also visible. UCLA Histology Collection.

title: Bone / Cartilage | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Between the bone spicules can be seen various bone cell types, including osteoblasts and osteoprogenitor cells. The left side of this image shows hypertrophied chondrocyte lacunae. UCLA Histology Collection.

title: Bone - Osteoclasts and Osteocytes | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Osteoclasts are cells with multiple nuclei which result from the fusion of many monocytes. Osteocytes are cells which have differentiated from osteoblasts and have surrounded themselves with bone. UCLA Histology Collection.

title: Cells / Organelles - Developing Bone | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Another area of the newborn rat knee, demonstrating a portion of developing bone, stained pinkish. The cells producing the bone are called osteoblasts. Identify a nucleus, nucleolus. The Golgi apparatus can be identified as the clear, central area. UCLA Histology Collection.

title: Survey and detail of bone marrow section (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: modified hematoxylin and eosin (A, B). The bone marrow consists of bone trabecles or crests (1) covered with osteoclasts and osteoblasts. Between the trabecles bone marrow parenchym (2) consisting of progenitor cells, reticular cells and fat cells (3). Numerous capillaries (B, 4) and enlarged sinusoids (B, 5) are present in the reticular tissue.

title: Bone | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Intramembranous bone formation. In the fetal skull, plates of bone are laid down in the mesenchymal field. This image shows woven or immature bone, which tends to be more cellular than lamellar or adult bone. Osteoprogenitor cells differentiate into osteoblasts, which produce the osteoid or uncalcified bone. Once the bone is calcified the osteocytes are trapped in the bone matrix. Osteoclasts continue to remodel the bone as necessary. UCLA Histology Collection.
